chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from Sulayman ibn Amr, who said: 'Imran ibn Abu Ata' narrated to me, saying: Ata' narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

He said: There is no word of speech more beloved to Allah, the Mighty and High, than 'La ilaha illa Allah' (There is no god but Allah). And there is no servant who says 'La ilaha illa Allah' and prolongs his voice with it until he finishes, except that his sins are scattered beneath his feet as the leaves of a tree are scattered beneath it.

key_terms.تَنَاثَرَتْ ذُنُوبُهُ: His sins are scattered/dispersed (expiation of sins)
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah (the declaration of monotheism)
key_terms.وَرَقُ الشَّجَرِ: Leaves of the tree (simile for the ease of sins falling away)
key_terms.يَمُدُّ بِهَا صَوْتَهُ: He prolongs his voice with it (reciting with emphasis and length)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for reciting 'La ilaha illa Allah' with devotion?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, this narration highlights the metaphysical weight of *La ilaha illa Allah* as the ultimate key to divine forgiveness, linking verbal declaration with spiritual purification. The imagery of sins scattering like leaves underscores the transformative power of sincere, prolonged recitation (*tadhyil*) in Shia devotional practice, serving as a potent reminder of God's mercy for the monotheist.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 14. `Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Qummi (my father) (ra) related us that Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah reported, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Sayf, on the authority of Sulayman ibn `Amru said: `Imran ibn Abu `Ata’ said: `Ata’ related on the authority of Ibn `Abbas that the Prophet (sw) said:

There is no statement more loved to Allah, the Mighty and High, than `There is no god but Allah.’ There is not a single servant (of Allah) who pronounces these words but that his sins are dispersed under his feet like the leaves of a tree are scattered beneath it.
